key_insight: Robot demonstrations can convey task steps and object roles rather than scene-specific appearances. This semantic view suggests a way to transfer manipulation skills across environments through in-context learning instead of encoding every skill in network weights.
problem_solved: Trained robot policies are tied to their training distributions, while in-context learning has lagged because demonstrations from other scenes lack feedback from the robot’s current environment.
method: Use manipulation demonstrations as in-context experience rather than relying solely on skills stored in policy weights.
Represent transferable experience through semantic task steps and object roles, not visual appearance.
Motivate grounding transferred experience in the current world; the supplied abstract is truncated before the implementation details.
impact: This direction could make robot skills more reusable across changing environments and reduce reliance on retraining. The supplied excerpt does not establish performance gains or evaluation results.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: skills stored in network weights versus demonstrations supplied in context.
Two visually different scenes linked by the same object roles and task sequence.
Feedback-loop diagram showing a robot interacting with its current environment.
Step icons illustrating a manipulation sequence: identify, grasp, move, place.
paper_title: World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation
paper_authors: Heng Fang, Zehui Guo, Yuehan Zhang, Mingyang Du, Dingkang Liang
